title: Voice Turn: instant endpointing and barge-in
one_liner: A voice assistant that answers the moment a request is complete, instead of waiting for a fixed silence timeout, and stops talking when the speaker interrupts.
what_it_does: The user presses Start. A simulated microphone plays a scripted transcript of ten utterances with realistic per-word timing, or a live microphone streams partial transcripts. On every new word the app sends the transcript so far to the judge and asks "has the speaker finished a complete request?", "what do they want?", and, while the assistant speaks, "is the speaker interrupting?". Slot questions (timer duration, room, contact) only appear when a regex finds candidates in the transcript; the judge picks one candidate or "none". Code owns all thresholds: fire when turn_complete >= 0.85 and the pause is >= 250 ms; if turn_complete < 0.35 the silence fallback stretches to 2500 ms; otherwise a 1000 ms silence timeout applies; with no answer at all the plain timeout applies. When it fires, a canned reply from intent plus slot is spoken by TTS. If is_barge_in >= 0.8 while speaking, speech stops. A timeline strip shows the waveform, words, the turn_complete step line, a green "fired" marker, an orange "silence baseline would fire" marker, a shaded "saved" band and a red barge-in marker. Panels show judge latency p50/p95, requests, tokens, cost, and a comparison of mean delay after end of speech: 1000 ms baseline vs about 350 ms with the judge, plus cut-off count, fires/fallbacks, saved per turn and cumulative. A Turns table lists intent, slot, probability at fire, delay and saving, tagged BARGED or BASELINE CUT OFF.

jev_questions.instructions: Has the speaker finished saying a complete request, so that the assistant should respond right now instead of waiting for more words? Judge from `transcript_so_far` and the pause length `ms_since_last_word`. criteria.true: The words form a complete, self-contained request or statement. Nothing essential is missing; an assistant could act on it as-is. criteria.false: The speaker is mid-sentence: the transcript ends on a dangling word (for, to, in, the, and, a, of), names an action without its object, or is clearly about to add more.
jev_questions.state_shape: {context, transcript_so_far, ms_since_last_word, word_count, assistant_state: listening|speaking, assistant_is_saying?}

jev_questions.instructions: What does the speaker want the assistant to do, based on `transcript_so_far`?
options: set_timer: Start a timer, alarm or countdown for a duration
weather: Ask about weather, temperature or forecast
play_music: Play a song, artist, genre or playlist
lights: Turn lights on/off, dim, or change their color
send_message: Send a text or message to a person
question: A general knowledge or factual question
chit_chat: Greeting, small talk or thanks with no task
incomplete: Too little said so far to tell what the speaker wants

jev_questions.instructions: The assistant is currently speaking the text in `assistant_is_saying`. Is the speaker interrupting to make the assistant stop, be quiet, cancel, or change what it is doing? criteria.true: Words like stop, wait, no, cancel, never mind, shut up, hold on, or a brand new request that overrides the current response. criteria.false: Silence, filler (uh, hmm), backchannel agreement (ok, yeah, thanks), or the speaker echoing the assistant.
jev_questions.state_shape: same state, only sent while assistant_state == speaking

jev_questions.instructions: Which of these phrases from the transcript is the duration the speaker wants the timer set for?
options: none: None of them is the timer duration
jev_questions.state_shape: same state, only when duration regex matches

jev_questions.instructions: Which room does the speaker want the lights command applied to?
options: <matched rooms from list kitchen, bedroom, living room, bathroom, office, garage, hallway, dining room, basement, nursery, porch>
jev_questions.state_shape: same state, only when a room word is present

jev_questions.instructions: Who does the speaker want to send the message to?
jev_questions.state_shape: same state, only when contact regex matches

request_cadence: One fan-out request per partial transcript update (roughly per word, every 250-400 ms while speaking), coalesced to at most one in flight. Measured: 58 requests per 75 s session, about 1.4 decisions/s while speaking, ~697 input tokens per request. HTTP 429 triggers a 2 s backoff.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"text":"set a timer for ten","statement":"The speaker has finished a complete request the assistant can act on now.","when_true":"The words form a complete, self-contained request. Nothing essential is missing.","when_false":"The transcript ends mid-sentence on a dangling word like for, to, in, the, and, or names an action without its object."} -> {answer, probability}
dm1_mapping.notes: text is the raw partial transcript only. Do not put ms_since_last_word in text; the 250 ms min-pause guard and the 1000/2500 ms timeouts live in code, as in TurnPolicy. Use probability against fireThreshold 0.85 and incompleteThreshold 0.35. Sent once per coalesced partial while listening.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /yes-no {"text":"Assistant is saying: \"Turning the living room lights on.\" Speaker says: \"stop stop\"","statement":"The speaker interrupts to make the assistant stop, cancel, or change what it is doing.","when_true":"Words like stop, wait, no, cancel, never mind, hold on, or a brand new request that overrides the response.","when_false":"Filler (uh, hmm), backchannel agreement (ok, yeah, thanks), or the speaker echoing the assistant."} -> {answer, probability}
dm1_mapping.notes: Only sent while phase == speaking; replaces the turn_complete call for that partial. Threshold 0.8. If barge-in fires, send one turn_complete yes-no on the interruption text to decide whether it is a new request (>= 0.85) or just a stop.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text":"set a timer for ten minutes","labels":{"set_timer":"Start a timer, alarm or countdown for a duration","weather":"Ask about weather, temperature or forecast","play_music":"Play a song, artist, genre or playlist","lights":"Turn lights on/off, dim, or change their color","send_message":"Send a text or message to a person","question":"A general knowledge or factual question","chit_chat":"Greeting, small talk or thanks with no task","incomplete":"Too little said so far to tell what the speaker wants"}} -> {label, probability, scores}
dm1_mapping.notes: Sent once at fire time (not per partial) to save budget. Optionally also every 3rd partial for the live intent readout, if the budget allows. Map label to Intent enum; unknown -> incomplete.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text":"set a timer for ten minutes","labels":{"ten minutes":"This phrase is the duration the speaker wants the timer set for","none":"None of the phrases is the timer duration"}} -> {label}
dm1_mapping.notes: Labels are the regex duration candidates plus none (classify needs >= 2 labels, so none is always present). Sent at fire time only when intent == set_timer and candidates exist. Code copies the label verbatim; nothing generated.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text":"turn off the lights in the kitchen","labels":{"kitchen":"The room the lights command applies to","none":"No specific room is named"}} -> {label}
dm1_mapping.notes: Sent at fire time when intent == lights and a room word matched. Cheaper alternative: one POST /entities {text, types:{duration:"a length of time for a timer", room:"a room in a house", contact:"a person to message"}} at fire time replaces all three slot calls; prefer this if latency matters more than fidelity to the candidate-selection design.

dm1_mapping.dm1_body: POST /classify {"text":"text mom I'll be late","labels":{"mom":"The person the message is for","none":"No recipient is named"}} -> {label}
dm1_mapping.notes: Sent at fire time when intent == send_message and the contact regex matched.

browser_plan: Build a Vite/React page at demo.milliseconds.ai/voice-turn in the milliseconds site style (dark panels, mono numerics, green = judge, orange = baseline, red = barge-in). Sources: (1) Simulated microphone, default, plays DemoScript with the same gapBeforeMs/durationMs via setTimeout and a synthetic level envelope; (2) Live microphone via Web Speech API (webkitSpeechRecognition, continuous, interimResults) when the browser supports it, with the same "audio never leaves the machine, only transcript text is sent" note; Chrome sends audio to Google, so word the note honestly. Assistant replies use speechSynthesis; cancel() on barge-in. Port TurnPolicy, CandidateExtractor, mergeWords, LatencyStats, TimelineMath 1:1 to TypeScript. Render the timeline strip on a canvas at 30 fps with requestAnimationFrame driving tick(). Proxy: a tiny serverless function (Cloudflare Worker or Vercel edge) at /api/dm1/:route that forwards JSON to https://api.milliseconds.ai/v1/decision-machine-1/:route with the server-side bearer key, allowlists routes, and passes back x-inference-ms and x-input-tokens headers plus the 429 status. Budget: the original sent up to 5 questions per partial as one fan-out; here send one /yes-no per coalesced partial (turn_complete while listening, is_barge_in while speaking), and defer intent classify and slot classify (or a single /entities) to fire time. Keep at most one request in flight, add a 500 ms minimum spacing (token bucket 2/s) so a burst of fast words coalesces, and discard stale answers by sequence number. That yields about 1 req/s during speech and 2-3 extra per turn at fire; the 10-utterance script stays near 60-70 requests per session, same as the original. On 429: 2 s backoff, banner "rate limited, silence fallback active", the policy falls back to the 1000 ms timeout so the demo never stalls. Show x-inference-ms as the latency source next to wall-clock RTT. Cost panel: use the milliseconds token price instead of the Jev figure.
risks: Short imperatives like 'text mom I'll be late' scored 0.42-0.55 on Jev; the yes-no statement may also land in the unsure band, so keep the silence fallback and expect 1-2 fallbacks per session.

Per-partial cadence is the whole point of the demo; with a shared 200 req/min org budget, two simultaneous visitors at ~1 req/s each already use most of it. Add a per-page 2 req/s cap and consider a proxy-side global limiter that returns 429 early.
Web Speech API interim results are jumpy and revise earlier words; the mergeWords logic must handle shrinking transcripts. Safari support is partial; keep simulated mode as the default.
Chrome Web Speech sends audio to Google servers; the on-device privacy claim from the macOS app does not hold in the browser. Reword the privacy note.

Judging turn completeness from text alone, without ms_since_last_word in the request, may lower recall for utterances that end on a noun and could continue. Validate the fire delay and cut-off counts against the README numbers before publishing.
speechSynthesis on some browsers needs a user gesture first and may not fire onend reliably; guard the speaking phase with a timeout so barge-in tests still run.
